risks.title: Persistent Inflationary Pressures
risks.summary: Inflation remains elevated above central bank targets, driven by supply shocks (energy, tariffs) and strong demand in certain sectors (AI). This necessitates continued tight monetary policy, posing a risk to growth.
risks.watch_for: CPI and PCE data releases, Federal Reserve statements on inflation outlook.
sources: Federal Reserve (FOMC statement, July 29 2026)
IMF (World Economic Outlook, April 2026)
Guggenheim Investments (Macro Themes for 2026)
KPMG (Economic Compass - Spring thaw, summer heat, June 10 2026)
Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midyear Outlook)
World Bank (Global Economic Prospects, June 2026)

risks.title: Geopolitical Tensions and Conflict Escalation
risks.summary: Ongoing conflicts, particularly in the Middle East, are driving energy price volatility, disrupting supply chains, and increasing global uncertainty, which weighs on economic activity and could lead to further inflationary pressures.
risks.watch_for: Developments in the Middle East conflict, oil price movements, and related supply chain disruptions.
sources: Federal Reserve (FOMC statement, July 29 2026)
IMF (World Economic Outlook, April 2026)
World Bank (Global Economic Prospects, June 2026)
KPMG (Economic Compass - Running on Empty?, April 08 2026)
Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midyear Outlook)

risks.title: US Fiscal Deficits and Rising National Debt
risks.summary: Sustained large federal budget deficits and a rising national debt increase borrowing costs and reduce fiscal space, posing long-term risks to economic stability and growth.
risks.watch_for: CBO's updated budget projections, Congressional budget negotiations.
sources: Congressional Budget Office (Budget and Economic Outlook, February 11 2026)
KPMG (Economic Compass - Rolling a boulder uphill, July 08 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch)

risks.title: AI Investment Boom and Productivity Lag
risks.summary: While AI investment is a significant growth driver, the full productivity benefits are yet to materialize, and the associated costs are currently contributing to inflation. A reevaluation of AI expectations could pose a risk.
risks.watch_for: Data on AI capital expenditures, productivity growth figures, and corporate earnings reports.
sources: JPMorgan (Mid-Year Outlook 2026)
Guggenheim Investments (Macro Themes for 2026)
KPMG (Economic Compass - Spring thaw, summer heat, June 10 2026)
Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midyear Outlook)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch)
World Bank (Global Economic Prospects, June 2026)

risks.title: Monetary Policy Uncertainty and Dissent
risks.summary: The Federal Reserve faces a delicate balancing act between controlling inflation and supporting growth. Dissenting views within the FOMC and potential shifts in policy approach create uncertainty for markets.
risks.watch_for: FOMC meeting minutes and statements, Federal Reserve Chair's speeches.
sources: Federal Reserve (FOMC statement, July 29 2026)
Guggenheim Investments (The Outlook for 2026 Is Positive Despite Challenges, June 22 2026)
Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midyear Outlook)
Maryland Daily Record (Fed holds rates steady; three policymakers dissent in favor of hike, July 29 2026)
Trading Economics (United States Fed Funds Interest Rate, August 03 2026)

risks.title: Tariff Uncertainty and Trade Policy Shifts
risks.summary: Ongoing tariff disputes and potential policy shifts create uncertainty for businesses and consumers, impacting trade flows, investment decisions, and contributing to inflationary pressures.
risks.watch_for: Announcements of new tariffs, trade negotiations, and their impact on import/export data.
sources: JPMorgan (Mid-Year Outlook 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch)
KPMG (Economic Compass - Spring thaw, summer heat, June 10 2026)
KPMG (Economic Compass - Running on Empty?, April 08 2026)

risks.title: Labor Market Resilience and Affordability Concerns
risks.summary: While the labor market has shown resilience, concerns about affordability persist for consumers, particularly regarding housing, energy, and healthcare costs, which could impact spending and economic growth.
risks.watch_for: Unemployment rate, wage growth, consumer confidence surveys, and inflation in key household budget categories.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch)
Guggenheim Investments (Macro Themes for 2026)
KPMG (Economic Compass - Spring thaw, summer heat, June 10 2026)
Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midyear Outlook)

risks.title: Global Growth Slowdown and EM Vulnerabilities
risks.summary: Global growth is projected to slow, with emerging market and developing economies facing particular headwinds due to conflict, commodity price volatility, and tighter financial conditions.
risks.watch_for: Global GDP growth forecasts, emerging market economic indicators, and commodity price trends.
sources: IMF (World Economic Outlook, April 2026)
World Bank (Global Economic Prospects, June 2026)

consensus_note: There is a broad consensus that persistent inflation, driven by supply shocks and strong demand, remains a primary concern, necessitating careful monetary policy navigation. Geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Middle East, are seen as a significant downside risk, exacerbating inflation and supply chain issues. While AI investment is a key growth driver, its full productivity benefits are still unfolding, and its costs are contributing to inflation. Outlooks diverge slightly on the pace of disinflation and the precise path of Fed policy, with some anticipating a more gradual return to target inflation.
